A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAFA-SNN and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on five datasets, Jetson energy and runtime measurements, component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments comparing surrogate gradients, residual architectures, soft-subnetwork methods, projection methods and ANN resource requirements.

M1.justification: Equation (7) changes the reported threshold update from subtracting A(r_new-r_base) to adding it, reversing its feedback direction. This is a localized procedural correction. The three components, ZOO estimator, loss and prototype-projection rule remain; Algorithm 1 also clarifies the previously described base-training and incremental-learning stages.

E1.justification: The five FSCIL datasets and classification tasks remain CIFAR-100, MiniImageNet, CIFAR10-DVS, DVS128 Gesture and N-Caltech101. Added studies vary methods, architectures and evaluation settings within retained coverage rather than introduce another benchmark or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with FSLL, SoftNet and WSN in Table 12; six surrogate gradients in Table 17; and Subspace-reg in Table 18. Table 19 newly evaluates ANN versions of ASP, CoACT and PriViLege, extending beyond v1's SNN-adapted comparisons. The principal existing comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 changes the reported neuromorphic batch sizes from 128 throughout to 32 for CIFAR10-DVS and 8 for DVS128 Gesture and N-Caltech101. Added evaluations introduce SEW ResNet-18/34/50 configurations, pretrained ANN versus SNN comparisons, and peak-memory and projection-execution-time measurements. The PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun under the revised batch sizes.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original component ablations, shot counts, hyperparameter sweeps and firing-rate analyses, v2 directly tests ZOO against six surrogate gradients and compares projection mechanisms. It also investigates depth degradation using SEW residual architectures and training-time scalability across additional architectures.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions with different seeds and use the same existing uncertainty-reporting format. Additional tables extend that practice without introducing a new run-count policy, confidence-interval procedure or significance test.

E6.justification: The principal retained scores remain unchanged, including Table 1's MiniImageNet final accuracies of 48.70% for SAFA-SNN and 44.69% for CLOSER. Substantial new results appear in Tables 11, 12, 15 and 17–19. For example, Table 17 reports 50.13% final accuracy with ZOO versus 46.71% with the triangle surrogate. These are added comparisons, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 revises the MSE bound from O(delta^2)+O(b delta^2 d^2) to O(delta^2)+O(d/(b delta^2)), and replaces convergence to the original gradient with convergence to the smoothed-objective gradient. Appendix D substantively revises the transformed-density and surrogate-recovery derivations. New Appendix E introduces noise assumptions, error decomposition and covariance bounds. v1's extended continuous-time IF/LIF derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The first general on-device SNN FSCIL contribution, three-component approach and claimed 4.01-point MiniImageNet advantage remain. The abstract modestly narrows the energy claim by explicitly locating the 20% reduction on CIFAR-100.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the suggestion that deeper networks need more epochs with an identity-mapping explanation and SEW residual remedy. It expands explanations of homeostatic preservation, prototype projection and ZOO overhead, discusses pretraining differences in ANN comparisons, and newly interprets the retained misclassification results as evidence that projection introduces no additional bias.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability link, dataset sizes and image resolutions, fuller baseline-adaptation descriptions, and clarification that the initialization mask remains fixed. These improve documentation; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents. Core hardware, optimizer and epoch information was already present.

R1.justification: The positioning expands substantially through comparisons with soft-subnetwork learning, surrogate-gradient training, trainable subspace regularization and ANN PEFT approaches. Added references and discussion connect neuronal dynamics to homeostatic plasticity and distinguish the method from FSLL, SoftNet, WSN and Subspace-reg. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The introduction, methodological motivation, neuronal-dynamics explanation and several appendix discussions are extensively rewritten. The appendix changes from A.1–A.16 to separately organized A–T sections, with revised baseline descriptions and navigation. Section 6.4, acknowledgments and an LLM-use disclosure are added, alongside affiliation and terminology edits.

P2.justification: Six new tables present the added comparisons, while retained tables are relocated and reformatted. Figures 4 and 5 are redrawn with different styling, legends and axes, including a truncated energy axis in Figure 4. Other figures receive labeling refinements, and Algorithm 1 is restructured and relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, targeted component and depth comparisons, clearer treatment of smoothed gradients, and explicit code-access information improve evaluability and reproducibility. However, new Table 18 reverses WARP's average and final-session values relative to retained Table 4, reducing confidence in the expanded comparisons. The revision provides a useful but qualified net quality improvement.
